name: Pool
description: How a Pool hands out warm Sandboxes, and what a checkout leaves behind.

scenarios.title: Construction builds no Sandbox
given: a setup block that counts the pooled Sandboxes it prepares
scenarios.then: the setup block has not run

scenarios.title: The checkout wait has a default bound
given: a Pool constructed without `checkout_timeout:`
scenarios.when: the default checkout wait bound is read

scenarios.title: An idle Sandbox is preferred over a new one
given: a Pool with `slots: 2`
a completed checkout that left its Sandbox idle
scenarios.then: the block receives the Sandbox the first checkout held

scenarios.title: Setup prepares a Sandbox, not a checkout
given: a Pool with `slots: 2` and a setup block that records each Sandbox it prepares
scenarios.then: the setup block has run once

scenarios.title: Sandbox keywords reach the Sandboxes the Pool builds
given: a Pool constructed with `slots: 1` and `timeout: 0.05`
scenarios.when: a checked-out Sandbox evaluates a non-terminating loop

scenarios.title: A setup failure surfaces where it was triggered
given: a Pool whose setup block raises on its first run
scenarios.then: the setup block's own exception reaches the `#with` caller unchanged

scenarios.title: A failed construction does not consume its slot
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
a first checkout whose construction failed in the setup block
scenarios.then: the checkout succeeds and the block's value comes back

scenarios.title: Checkout answers with what the caller computed
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
scenarios.when: `Pool#with` runs with a block returning a value

scenarios.title: Setup registrations outlive the checkout that first used them
given: a Pool whose setup block binds a Service on each Sandbox it prepares
a completed checkout that reached that Service
scenarios.when: a later checkout evaluates guest code naming the same Service
scenarios.then: the Service returns its value to the guest

scenarios.title: Guest state does not travel between holders
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
a completed checkout that set a guest global variable
scenarios.when: a later checkout reads that global

scenarios.title: A full Pool makes the caller wait rather than refuse
given: a Pool with `slots: 1` whose only Sandbox is held by another thread
a checkout blocked waiting for it
scenarios.when: the holder checks its Sandbox back in
scenarios.then: the blocked checkout completes and returns its block's value

scenarios.title: A nested checkout is an ordinary second holder
given: a Pool with `slots: 2`
a running `Pool#with` block on this thread
scenarios.then: the inner block receives a different Sandbox than the outer one

scenarios.title: A trapped Sandbox is never handed out again
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
a checkout whose block raised `Kobako::TrapError`
scenarios.then: the block receives a different Sandbox than the one the trap left

scenarios.title: The refilled slot is a working one
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
a checkout whose block raised `Kobako::TrapError`
scenarios.when: the next checkout's Sandbox evaluates guest code

scenarios.title: Refilling builds a Sandbox rather than reviving one
given: a Pool with `slots: 1` and a setup block that records each Sandbox it prepares
a checkout whose block raised `Kobako::TrapError`
scenarios.then: the setup block has run twice

scenarios.title: Only a trap costs the Pool its Sandbox
given: a Pool with `slots: 1`
a checkout whose block raised `Kobako::SandboxError`
scenarios.then: the block receives the Sandbox that error left

scenarios.title: A guest error costs no construction
given: a Pool with `slots: 1` and a setup block that records each Sandbox it prepares
a checkout whose block raised `Kobako::SandboxError`
scenarios.then: the setup block has run once

scenarios.title: Reachability is the whole of the lifecycle
given: a Pool that has constructed one Sandbox
no remaining Host App reference to either
scenarios.then: the Pool and the Sandbox are both reclaimed

scenarios.title: A holder outlives the Pool it borrowed from
given: a running `Pool#with` block that has dropped the last Pool reference and run a collection
scenarios.when: the checked-out Sandbox evaluates guest code inside that block

text: A Pool is observable in three places: which Sandbox a checkout receives,
how many times the setup block has prepared one, and whether a slot survives
what its holder did with it. Each scenario settles one of those and stops.
The checkout wait bound and the constructor's argument validation raise rather
than answer, so they belong to the error taxonomy and are specified there.
That a pooled Sandbox satisfies every other behavior identically to a directly
constructed one is a claim about the whole corpus rather than a difference one
observation settles; the isolation scenarios above are its pool-side witnesses.
